A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVGGT work. All 11 pages of each, including equations, four figures, six tables, and references, are readable and comparable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original MVRefer evaluations, component and configuration ablations in Tables 1–6, and qualitative predictions in Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original MVRefer evaluations, ablations, and qualitative predictions, including MVGGT's 39.9 overall global mIoU.

M1.justification: Both retain the frozen Pi3 reconstruction backbone, frozen language encoder, 12-block multimodal branch, geometric and language injection, mask reconstruction procedure, and BCE-plus-PVSO objective. Sections 4–5.1 disclose no procedural or architectural revision.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same sparse-view MVRefer task constructed from ScanRefer and ScanNet, with Hard/Easy and Unique/Multiple categories. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain ReferDINO/Pi3-based 2D-Lift, Pi3/LESS-based two-stage, and the same seven traditional 3D-RES comparators. Newly cited methods in related work are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain eight-view sampling with target-visibility replacement, standard ScanRefer splits, the 5% difficulty threshold, evaluation metrics, training budget, and ablation configurations. Section 5.1's settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 3–6 test the same core components, PVSO sampling and suppression, fusion placement, and branch depth. Figure 4 retains the same five qualitative examples. Rewritten discussion introduces no additional analytical experiment or evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 5.3 corrects the Hard-split comparison attributed to MVGGT from 12.9→19.0 to 19.0→24.4 global mIoU, matching the unchanged Table 3 rows. Other tabulated results are retained; Table 4's 66.51→66.5 is equivalent rounding, not a performance change.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 retain the same task and metric definitions, attention operations, Dice-gradient derivation, sampling ratio, suppression weighting, and training objective. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: MV-3DRES, MVGGT, the FGD diagnosis and PVSO remedy, and MVRefer. Condensation does not alter their central novelty or performance claims.

C2.justification: The component discussion corrects attribution of the Hard-split gain. Section 5.3 also changes the depth-degradation explanation from 'pointing to' overfitting to 'due to' overfitting without additional evidence. Section 5.4 reframes example (c) from depth-noise recovery to resolving semantic distraction.

D1.justification: v1 explicitly states that code and models are publicly available; v3 mentions only code at the same project site. This narrows the resource disclosure without establishing that models were withdrawn. Implementation and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 55 to 68 works, adding citations such as 3DREST, Grounded 3D-LLM, Transcrib3D, ViewRefer, and Omni-view in Section 2.1. Literature coverage broadens, but the positioning narrative and claimed distinction from prior work remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 and 6 undergo substantial rewriting and condensation, including replacing detailed qualitative-example explanations with a compact summary. Earlier scientific sections largely retain their wording and order. Author information is updated and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained. Ablation-table typography is adjusted, notably enlarging Table 4's text; Table 6 moves between columns on PDF page 8. Figure 2's caption typo is corrected, and surrounding text and references reflow.

improvement.justification: Correcting the Table 3 attribution improves reporting accuracy, while clearer ablation-table typography and broader literature coverage provide modest benefits. These gains are limited by reduced case-specific explanation, stronger unsupported causal wording about overfitting, and omission of the explicit model-availability statement. The revision improves presentation and reporting modestly without strengthening the empirical evidence.
